newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends sharply lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends sharply lower on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil prices plunged Thursday after a sell-off in gas oil futures in London accelerated profit-taking started Wednesday, with crude and gasoline retracing gains made on heat's recent torrid rise.
"It was a correction that was overdue. There was a lot of length getting out," said a trader.

November heating oil settled off 3.05 cents at 70.92 cents a gallon. November gas oil on London's IPE settled $13.75 lower at 225.00 a tonne. Profit-taking started Wednesday after the American Petroleum Institute reported a larger-than-expected build in distillate inventories.

Traders said the correction was mostly over since heating oil's losses in the past two days have created a 50 percent correction from the latest short-term uptrend which started with a breakout mid-September.
Corrections usually lop off one-half to two thirds of the most previous uptrend.

November crude settled 81 cents lower at $24.26 a barrel and November gasoline ended 2.07 cents lower at 63.52 cents a gallon. Crude got some support on news OPEC is likely to hold its oil output quota at 25.03 million bpd, but the news was not bullish enough to buffer heat's downdraft, traders said.
"Heating oil was the large factor. It was too bearish for the OPEC news," said a trader.

Over the past three months, the price of heating oil's spot month has risen more than 30 percent on historically low supplies. Dealers said heating oil inventories remain tight and will buoy oil prices longer term.
Heating oil inventories are 17 million barrels below year ago.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
